description.narrative: Projet Japon Bossangoa.In the Central African Republic (CAR), the number of people in need of assistance has increased across all sectors between 2022 and 2023, ranging from food security, and nutrition to WASH (water, sanitation, and hygiene), protection and GBV. In 2023, 3.4 million people (56 % of the population) need humanitarian assistance and protection, up 10 % compared to 2022. Soaring food insecurity is one of the major causes of vulnerability and distress for the population in CAR, which has one of the highest rates of food insecurity in the world, with 50% of the population not eating enough. These challenges are pertinent in Bossangoa, the capital of the Ouham Prefecture in the North-West region of the Central African Republic. Once known as the “bread basket” of CAR, successive crises, lack of investment, rapid population growth coupled with external shocks such as global inflation, climate change and the influx of displacement have severely hampered the agricultural production capacity of the region. Of the households practising agriculture, 97% noted difficulties and expected a decrease in their harvest. The challenges in terms of food insecurity are compounded by the decrease in purchasing power due to global inflation, lack of livelihood opportunities, and lack of access to basic services, especially water. Given the complexity and multidimensional nature of the needs in Bossangoa, this project uses an area-based approach that seeks to provide a holistic response and aims to i) improve access to basic services, particularly access to drinking water, ii) increase income opportunities and support local economic reactivation, particularly through improved agricultural production, and iii) strengthen social cohesion.
